scenes.title: CloudHSM dedicated HSM cluster
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains cloudhsm dedicated hsm cluster by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

Start with the application client using PKCS number eleven, JCE or CNG cryptographic libraries. Follow the arrow into the VPC-based CloudHSM cluster spanning two Availability Zones. Keys are generated and used inside dedicated HSMs, with cluster synchronization and encrypted backups supporting availability and recovery. The bottom panels distinguish responsibilities: AWS operates the hardware, but you manage crypto users, keys, cluster configuration and application integration. Multi-AZ deployment helps resilience but does not replace workload testing.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Use CloudHSM for dedicated hardware control when its additional operational burden is justified.

scenes.title: Direct CloudHSM or KMS custom key store
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains direct cloudhsm or kms custom key store by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

Compare the alternatives from left to right. With direct CloudHSM, application code calls HSM client libraries and you manage crypto integration, HSM users and key operations. With a CloudHSM-backed KMS custom key store, the application or supported AWS service calls familiar KMS APIs, and the KMS key uses your connected CloudHSM cluster. The latter preserves KMS permissions and integrations, but depends on your cluster's health, capacity and availability. Both options entail customer-managed HSM operations.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
Choose direct cryptographic control versus KMS API compatibility based on the integration requirement.

scenes.title: External KMS key store
scenes.visual_overview: This slide explains external kms key store by following the pictured security architecture.
visual_walkthrough: Identify the featured AWS service and the full context

An application or AWS service on the left invokes AWS KMS and undergoes normal authorization. The request crosses the trust boundary via a customer-operated external key store proxy, with secure mutual TLS communication to the outside key manager. That external manager holds the key material and performs supported cryptographic operations; results return through the proxy to KMS and the caller. The right-side operations checklist emphasizes proxy scaling, external service availability, latency and monitoring. Failure outside AWS can block dependent AWS KMS calls.
Distinguish permission, security and operational responsibilities
External key custody is a compliance trade-off that introduces availability and latency dependencies.
